ca_north_buttress_base_routes.blurb: A compact wall at the foot of Lower Cathedral Rock in Yosemite Valley, close to the Bridalveil Falls pullouts. Eleven routes, almost all of them trad with a single sport line and some two-pitch options, run from 5.9 into the 5.12 range, with the bulk sitting in the 5.10s. The wall faces mostly north and stays in shade through the day, so it suits warm afternoons and feels cold in winter. Expect a quick walk in from the road, short technical leads with some runout on the easier lines, and a standard rack plus a big cam for a chimney move.

ca_secret_garden.blurb: A sport-climbing wall in the upper reaches of Williamson Rock, in the San Gabriel Mountains of the Angeles National Forest. It is split into a lower half, which is steeper and holds the harder lines, and an upper half of slabby to vertical climbing with easier routes. All eleven routes are bolted, running from 5.9 up to the low 5.12s, with most of them in the 5.11 range. Sitting well above the main walls, it tends to be a quieter place, and the climbing is steep and technical, rewarding good footwork and stamina.

ca_north_rocks.blurb: A cluster of small craglets at the north end of Moonstone Beach, near Arcata and Eureka on the Humboldt coast. The eleven climbs mix five boulder problems, a couple of top ropes, two trad lines and two sport routes. Boulders are mostly on the easy side, while the roped climbs run from 5.10 into the 5.12s and 5.13. It is a short stroll up the sand from the main beach, and the rocks stay usable even when winter surf is pounding the shore, which makes it a handy after-work spot.

ca_three_pillars_area.blurb: A small bouldering zone in the Underground, high on Queen Mountain in Joshua Tree National Park. It is the first cluster of boulders reached on the long uphill walk in, which follows cairns over several rock bands. All eleven problems are on the gentle side: six are at the easiest grade, four are around V0, and one is V2, so it suits warm-ups and newer boulderers. Named boulders here are the Pillars of Nobility, Truth and Hope. The Underground's rock is smoother and edgier than the rest of the park, and the area sits among pines.
